title: Unified Inference: Q4 2026 Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing
author: Priya Nair
content:
h1. Unified Inference — Q4 2026 Product Overview, PRD, Design Specs, Roadmap & Pricing

Introduction
This document consolidates the product-level view for Redwood Inference's Unified Inference offering as we enter Q4 2026. It contains: a short product overview, prioritized product requirements (PRD), high-level design specifications required for engineering handoff, roadmap and themes for the next three quarters, pricing and packaging recommendations, and the release notes for the most recent public rollout (v1.3). The intended audience includes product, engineering, sales, solutions, and customer success.

Goals (Why this matters)
- Make it straightforward for engineering teams to adopt a single inference API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Reduce customer unit economics (USD/tokens) by 20% for common web-scale workloads via batching, caching, and quantization guidance.
- Provide predictable latency SLOs for mid-tail 95th percentile (p95) across supported model classes (causal, chat, embeddings).
- Enable enterprise adoption through packaging and pricing options that align to procurement cycles.

Audience
- Primary: Product, Engineering (serving runtime, infra), Sales, Solutions Engineering.
- Secondary: Customer Success, Finance, Legal.

Scope (in/out)
In scope:
- Unified inference API surface (text generation, chat, embeddings, rerank).
- Configurable routing policies (latency/cost/region).
- Redwood Optimize recommendations integrated into console and API.
- Pricing tiers and committed capacity contracts for Dedicated.

Out of scope (for this document):
- Low-level kernel implementation decisions (see eng-serving-runtime runtime-architecture).
- Research model training or new model creation.

Section 1 — Product Requirements (PRD)
Summary: The PRD below groups features into Must, Should, and Could for Q4 2026. Each requirement includes acceptance criteria, owner, and target milestone.

1.1 Must-have requirements
- Unified REST and SDK API parity across deployment modes
  - Acceptance criteria: identical request/response schema for hosted and dedicated deployments; SDK v2.1 exposes identical methods.
  - Owner: Eng SDK (owner: Ben Carter)
  - Target milestone: 2026-09-30
- Model routing and fallback policy primitives
  - Acceptance criteria: customers can define route priority (latency, cost, region), with documented behavior when capacity is exhausted (fallback to compatible quantized variant).
  - Owner: Runtime & Orchestration (owner: Maria Chen)
  - Target milestone: 2026-10-15
- Per-route latency and cost SLOs with traceable attribution
  - Acceptance criteria: Console shows p50/p95/p99 latency and per-token cost for each route; alerts fire when p95 > 1.5x target.
  - Owner: Observability (owner: Ravi Patel)
  - Target milestone: 2026-10-31

1.2 Should-have requirements
- Redwood Optimize in-console recommendations for batching and quantization profiles
  - Acceptance criteria: system produces prescriptive config suggestions and estimated cost savings for top 3 route templates.
  - Owner: Product: Redwood Optimize (owner: Aisha Malik)
  - Target milestone: 2026-11-15
- Private deployment on-prem packaging improvements (installer idempotence and KMS integrations)
  - Acceptance criteria: validated install in a reference on-prem environment; KMS key rotation documented.
  - Owner: Private Deployments (owner: Omar Haddad)
  - Target milestone: 2026-11-30

1.3 Could-have requirements
- Automatic workload-based routing recommendations (ML-driven)
  - Acceptance criteria: beta recommendations in console with confidence score; opt-in.
  - Owner: Applied ML (owner: Lina Gomez)
  - Target milestone: 2027-02-28

Non-functional requirements (NFRs)
- Security: support for customer KMS and HSM for Private deployments (CIS compliance baseline).
- Reliability: platform-level p99 availability >= 99.95% for hosted API.
- Performance: baseline p95 generation latency for 512-token causal tasks <= 120ms on Dedicated (single-request path).

Section 2 — Design specification (high-level)
This section provides the architecture and design constraints required for engineering to estimate and implement the features above. It is intended for engineering teams to create ADRs and design walkthroughs.

2.1 High-level architecture
- API Gateway: single public REST/SDK surface that normalizes requests and enforces auth/rate limits.
- Control Plane: configuration service storing routing policies, model catalog, and rollout definitions.
- Serving Plane: GPU-optimized runtime (continuous batching, KV cache, quantization paths).
- Observability & Telemetry: per-request tracing, token-level cost attribution, and model-quality hooks.

2.2 Key components and contracts
- Route config schema (JSON) — example snippet:
  "{"route_name":"low_latency","priority":["latency","region"],"fallbacks":["gptx-small-quant","gptx-medium-fp16"]}"
  - Contract: runtime must honor priority ordering and return fallback metadata in response headers.
- Cost attribution spec: token_cost = model_unit_price * (compute_factor + caching_factor); compute_factor derived from kernel selection logs.
  - Contract: console must reconcile billing with usage logs within 24 hours.

2.3 Rollout and migration constraints
- Backwards compatibility: new API fields must be additive. Deprecation windows: minimum 90 days with telemetry on callers.
- Migration: dedicated customers can pin old model versions; default for new customers is latest recommended model.

2.4 Operational runbook summary (for releases)
- Pre-Release: create canary pool (1% traffic), smoke tests for latency/cost/accuracy, update runbook.
- Release: 10% -> 50% -> 100% rollout with automated rollback on SLO breach (p95 spike or error rate > 0.5%).
- Post-Release: 72-hour monitoring period, postmortem if any SLO breached.

Section 3 — Roadmap & Themes (next 3 quarters)
Q4 2026 (current) — Reliability & Packaging
- Deliver per-route SLOs, routing primitives, Redwood Optimize recommendations, and pricing tiers for Dedicated.
- Theme: Production-readiness (SLA/Rollouts/Observability).

Q1 2027 — Cost Efficiency & Developer Experience
- Focus: autoscaling improvements, advanced caching (prefix-based), SDK ergonomics (type-safe clients), improved docs and quickstarts.
- Theme: Make low-cost serving configurations first-class.

Q2 2027 — Enterprise & Private Expansion
- Focus: expanded compliance evidence packages, air-gap installer, and partner marketplace listings.
- Theme: Sellability and procurement readiness.

OKR alignment (example)
- OKR 1 (Product): Increase self-serve conversion by 30% through improved quickstarts and default routing policies.
- OKR 2 (Engineering): Reduce average per-token compute by 18% for common workloads.

Section 4 — Pricing & Packaging Notes
Objective: align pricing to clear unit economics while enabling committed-seating contracts for customers with predictable throughput.

4.1 Pricing tiers (recommended)
- Developer (Self-serve Hosted)
  - $0.0009 / 1k tokens generation (baseline model catalog small-medium)
  - Free tier: 10k tokens/month and 30-day trial credits
  - Limits: rate-limited to protect multi-tenant pools
- Business (Standard Hosted + Limited Dedicated)
  - $0.0035 / 1k tokens generation for performance models
  - Optional Reserved Dedicated: starting at $8,000 / month commit (applies as credit)
- Enterprise (Dedicated + Private)
  - Custom pricing: reserved capacity pricing with step-down per-token rates at volume bands (example: >10B tokens/month -> $0.0018 per 1k tokens)
  - Add-ons: premium support, compliance package, extended observability retention

4.2 Packaging and contract recommendations
- Dedicated reservations: 12-month and 36-month commit options with tiered discounts and guaranteed capacity windows.
- Onboarding: 8-week onboarding for Private deployments with optional paid integration engineering.
- Billing: monthly invoicing with reconciliation reports; per-route cost breakdown exported to CSV for finance.

4.3 Pricing caveats and guardrails
- Pricing must be reconciled with observed on-platform egress & compute costs; product finance to validate target GP margins >= 65% for hosted plans.
- Special discounts for education/nonprofit to be handled by Sales (up to 25% off list).

Section 5 — Release Notes (v1.3, public rollout 2026-11-15)
Overview: v1.3 focuses on routing policies, in-console SLO dashboards, and Redwood Optimize beta recommendations.
Key user-facing changes:
- New route config UI and API: users can create route policies keyed by latency/cost/region.
- SLO dashboards per route with p50/p95/p99 and per-token cost attribution.
- Redwood Optimize: beta prescriptive suggestions for batching/quantization (opt-in).

Bug fixes and platform changes:
- Fixed a rare KV cache invalidation on long-running chat sessions.
- Reduced cold-start 95th percentile latency by optimizing kernel selection heuristics.
- Improved error messages and SDK parity across Python and Node clients.

Known issues:
- Embeddings costs for very large sequences (>2048 tokens) can be under-estimated in console for certain models (tracking: ENG-7122).
- Private installer occasionally times out behind strict proxy setups (workaround: configure http-proxy in installer; target fix 2026-12-05).

Rollout notes and operations summary:
- Canary: 2% traffic in us-west-2 for 24 hours with automated SLO checks.
- Full rollout: progressive 10/30/60 steps with 30-minute hold windows.
- Abort conditions: sustained 2x p95 increase for 15 minutes, increase in 5xx rate > 0.5% absolute.

Section 6 — Action items and ownership
- Product (Priya Nair): finalize pricing bands and GTM collateral by 2026-11-30.
- Engineering (Maria Chen): implement fallback policy contract and unit tests by 2026-10-15.
- Observability (Ravi Patel): dashboard and alert runbook completion by 2026-10-31.
- Private Deployments (Omar Haddad): validate on-prem installer in reference cluster by 2026-11-30.

Appendix A — Acceptance test checklist (sample)
1) API parity tests: run SDK parity suite across hosted and dedicated (pass rate 100%).
2) Routing and fallback: simulate capacity exhaustion, verify fallback model returned and metadata present.
3) Cost reconciliation: generate 1M tokens workload, validate console cost within 5% of internal billing.
4) Security: verify KMS integration and key rotation for Private deployment staging cluster.

Appendix B — Example config table
| Field | Type | Example | Notes |
| route_name | string | low_latency | unique id |
| priority | list | ["latency","region"] | priority order |
| fallbacks | list | ["gptx-small-quant"] | ordered fallback models |
| slo_p95_ms | integer | 120 | p95 target in ms |
| billing_code | string | route-frontend-01 | applied to cost reports |
